projects.title: AuthMatch AI
projects.tagline: Decision support for prior-authorization reviewers: matches each case to Medicare coverage policy and shows which criteria the documentation supports.
projects.description:
## The problem

Prior-authorization reviewers have to find the controlling Medicare coverage policy for each case and check the clinical documentation against it by hand. CMS-0057-F sets decision timeframes for this work, including seven calendar days for standard requests and 72 hours for expedited ones.

## What it does

AuthMatch AI matches each case, by procedure code and member state, to the applicable NCD or LCD policy and reads the documentation against it. The reviewer sees each criterion marked Met, Not Met or Indeterminate, with the supporting evidence cited. A qualified human reviewer makes every final decision; the AI never finalizes a case. It is decision support, not a coverage determination or a certification of regulatory compliance.

## Architecture

The Next.js reviewer interface proxies requests and does no PHI processing. Document processing, OCR, policy matching and LLM calls run in a separate FastAPI service. Postgres row-level security restricts data access, and an append-only, hash-chained audit log records case activity.

## Status

MVP. The web and API tiers are deployed.

projects.tagline: Turns a one-line project idea into the CLAUDE.md, PRD, and build plan your AI coding agents need.
projects.description:
## The problem

AI coding agents are only as good as the context you give them, and most projects have stale docs or none at all.

## What it does

From a one-line description of your project, Gen4Me researches your stack on the live web, asks you to confirm its assumptions instead of guessing, and generates a tailored CLAUDE.md, a research-backed PRD, a build plan, and per-directory rules. As the codebase evolves, it audits the docs against the code and flags drift.

## How it's built

Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and Postgres, with LLM pipelines grounded by live web research.

projects.tagline: Prototype that monitors sanctions updates from U.S., U.K., E.U. and U.N. authorities and turns them into summaries and alerts for compliance review.
projects.description:
## The problem

Sanctions lists change often across authorities, and compliance teams usually find out by reading raw regulatory text after the fact.

## What it does

SanctionsWatch collects updates from U.S., U.K., E.U. and U.N. sources on a schedule, deduplicates and classifies them, summarizes the impact with an LLM, and sends alerts. Compliance professionals decide applicability and action.

## Status

Prototype. The public deployment is not currently generating briefings.

## How it's built

Next.js and TypeScript on Supabase and Postgres, with an ingestion pipeline built on Apify.

projects.title: AI Engineering Factory & Analytics
projects.tagline: Built a supervised AI-assisted engineering system that coordinates planning, development, testing, independent review, and human release decisions, alongside a dashboard for delivery evidence and failure analysis.
projects.description:
## The problem

As a solo founder building multiple products, I needed more structured development capacity without losing control over code quality, security, ownership, or the release process.

## The system

I designed a governed workflow in which work is planned, assigned to specialized AI agents, isolated for implementation, checked through automated tests, reviewed independently, and presented for a human decision before release.

## The controls

Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.

## The analytics

A companion dashboard examines tasks, review outcomes, failures, timing, cost-related records where available, and evidence quality to make engineering performance more visible.

## What this demonstrates

Operating-system design for AI-assisted engineering; agent orchestration; quality governance; engineering metrics; traceability; and iterative improvement.

caseStudy.intro: Operating-system design for AI-assisted engineering; agent orchestration; quality governance; engineering metrics; traceability; and iterative improvement.
caseStudy.challenge: As a solo founder building multiple products, I needed more structured development capacity without losing control over code quality, security, ownership, or the release process.
caseStudy.delivered: I designed a governed workflow in which work is planned, assigned to specialized AI agents, isolated for implementation, checked through automated tests, reviewed independently, and presented for a human decision before release. A companion dashboard examines tasks, review outcomes, failures, timing, cost-related records where available, and evidence quality to make engineering performance more visible.
caseStudy.riskAndControls: Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.
caseStudy.howItWorks:
Every change moves through five phases.

**Govern and intake.** Requests from me, Jira or GitHub issues are reconciled into a ranked queue and revalidated before use. A task is picked only if it is unblocked, unclaimed and within the run budget, with up to three running in parallel.

**Triage and plan.** Work that is ready to build has an approved plan, clear acceptance criteria and bounded scope. Unclear or higher-risk work goes to planner agents, and a person reviews the plan. Missing information or conflicting requests are held for a person, never guessed.

**Build and validate.** One owner claims each task in its own isolated worktree. Specialist agents join only when needed. The implementer works inside the authorized scope and adds regression tests, then the project's quality gates run. Tests are never weakened to get a pass.

**Review and assure.** Independent reviewers run in parallel, chosen by what changed: code, security, AI behavior, UI and accessibility. Blocking findings get at most two repair cycles; then the system stops and asks.

**Approve and learn.** A passing change comes to me for approval before it merges into the protected main branch. Every run is recorded (hashes, not content) and feeds Factory Analytics (lead time, repair rate, review failure rate), which I use to tune the rules and agents.

Governance runs throughout: rules are enforced by hooks, high-risk work needs a person, secrets are scanned, and no agent approves its own work.
caseStudy.role: Designer and sole builder: operating model, agent roles, controls, tooling and analytics
caseStudy.keyDecisions:
- A person approves every change before it merges into the protected main branch; the system cannot merge on its own.
- One owner claims each task, and the work happens in its own isolated worktree, so parallel work cannot collide.
- Reviewers are chosen by what the change touches (code, security, AI behavior, UI and accessibility), not by judgment about whether review is needed.
- Blocking findings get at most two repair cycles; after that the system stops and asks a person.
- Tests are never weakened to obtain a pass.
- Run records store hashes, not content, so analytics never hold source code or prompts.
caseStudy.outcome: The Factory is in use on my own repositories, including the code behind this site. Run records feed Factory Analytics, a local dashboard that reports lead time, repair rate and review failure rate. The recorded sample is still small, so no performance figures are published here, and no claim is made of autonomous delivery or proven productivity gains.

projects.title: Enterprise Technology Operating Model Transformation
projects.tagline: Led the redesign of the Legal Technology product operating model at JPMorgan Chase: product taxonomy, ownership boundaries, decision rights and governance.
projects.description:
## The challenge

Legal Technology needed clear product boundaries, ownership and decision rights to strengthen accountability and strategic alignment across a global product portfolio.

## My responsibility

I led the redesign of the product operating model as Chief of Staff for Strategy & Execution, aligning roadmaps, resolving enterprise dependencies and strengthening portfolio governance. This was a leadership role exercised through influence across product, engineering, architecture, UX, site reliability, agility, finance, risk and Legal teams, not hands-on implementation.

## Key decisions

- Rationalized the product portfolio.
- Defined the product taxonomy and the ownership boundaries between products.
- Set decision rights and the governance that holds product owners accountable.
- Sponsored application and infrastructure modernization initiatives, including AWS cloud integration.

## What I delivered

A redesigned product operating model: a rationalized product portfolio with a defined taxonomy, ownership boundaries, decision rights and governance.

## Outcome and evidence

A rationalized portfolio with defined ownership and decision rights, designed to strengthen accountability and strategic alignment. Figures are omitted because they are employer-confidential.

projects.tagline: Owned JPMorgan Chase Legal Technology's annual strategy cycle, multi-year roadmap, OKRs, financial and workforce planning, and executive reporting.
projects.description:
## The challenge

Enterprise Legal, Technology and business priorities had to become portfolio objectives, product roadmaps, investment decisions, workforce plans and measurable execution commitments, and senior leaders needed reporting they could act on.

## My responsibility

I owned Legal Technology's annual strategy cycle and multi-year roadmap, established the annual OKR framework, and directed annual financial and workforce planning. I was the strategic advisor responsible for executive communications to JPMorgan's General Counsel and senior Technology leadership. This was a leadership role exercised through influence across product, engineering, architecture, UX, site reliability, agility, finance, risk and Legal teams, not hands-on implementation.

## Key decisions

- Translated enterprise priorities into portfolio objectives, product roadmaps, investment decisions, workforce plans and measurable execution commitments.
- Established the annual OKR framework, linking priorities to quarterly outcomes, portfolio commitments and executive performance reviews.
- Challenged forecasts, set headcount and location guardrails, and advised leaders on capacity, hiring, attrition and investment tradeoffs.

## What I delivered

The annual strategy and multi-year roadmap; the OKR framework; annual financial and workforce plans; and the executive operating rhythm: annual strategy presentations, quarterly business reviews, monthly operating reviews, portfolio dashboards, financial analyses and executive narratives.

## Outcome and evidence

Executive narratives, reviews and dashboards that shaped investment priorities and execution across the Legal Technology organization. Figures are omitted because they are employer-confidential.

projects.title: Enterprise AI Strategy & Governance
projects.tagline: Developed and operationalized the Legal Technology AI strategy at JPMorgan Chase: the AI book of work, governance model, use-case prioritization and adoption measures.
projects.description:
## The challenge

Legal Technology needed an AI strategy that connected opportunities across LLM assistants, knowledge and analytics platforms, document automation and AI-enabled legal workflows to prioritization, governance, accountability and measurable adoption.

## My responsibility

I developed and operationalized the Legal Technology AI strategy and directed annual risk, control and privacy readiness, including accountability for AI/ML-related business cases. This was a leadership role exercised through influence across product, engineering, architecture, UX, site reliability, agility, finance, risk and Legal teams, not hands-on implementation.

## Key decisions

- Established an AI book of work, so AI opportunities were managed as one prioritized portfolio.
- Set the governance model and the criteria for use-case prioritization.
- Defined adoption and ROI measures, and the executive reporting that tracked them.
- Clarified accountability for AI/ML-related business cases and drove governance, re-attestation, assessment and remediation activities.

## What I delivered

The AI book of work, the governance model, use-case prioritization, adoption and ROI measures, AI updates in executive reporting, and governance, re-attestation, assessment and remediation activities for AI/ML-related business cases.

## Outcome and evidence

An operating AI strategy: AI opportunities managed through one book of work with a governance model, prioritization, clarified accountability, and adoption and ROI measures reported to senior leadership. Figures are omitted because they are employer-confidential.

about.name: Erick Clark
about.title: Technology Strategy & AI Transformation Professional
about.heroTagline: Former Vice President and Chief of Staff for Legal Technology at JPMorgan Chase who also designs and builds working AI products. I understand technology from the executive decision to the working product.
bio: I understand technology from the executive decision to the working product. For more than 15 years I have worked on both sides of that line: deciding what an organization should invest in, and making sure what it builds actually works.

It started in the U.S. Army, where I served as an intelligence analyst. I turned complex, incomplete information into assessments and briefings that supported senior leaders' decisions, and I supervised and developed junior analysts. Clear analysis that ends in a clear recommendation still shapes how I work.

I then spent several years delivering technology in energy and technology services, at CenterPoint Energy, NRG Energy and CSAT Solutions: network infrastructure programs, billing and payment platforms, PMO governance and automation. Delivery taught me what a plan looks like once it meets engineering, vendors and operations.

At JPMorgan Chase, as Vice President and Chief of Staff for Legal Technology from 2019 to 2026, I worked on the decisions that shape delivery. I owned the annual strategy cycle and multi-year roadmap, led the redesign of the product operating model, directed financial and workforce planning, built the executive reporting for the General Counsel and senior Technology leadership, and developed the organization's AI strategy and governance model.

Since 2024 I have also designed and built AI products independently: AuthMatch AI for prior-authorization review, Prepera for career preparation, regulatory-monitoring tools, and a supervised AI engineering system that runs my own software delivery. Building them shows me where AI initiatives succeed or stall: data quality, controls, human review and the cost of operating them.
That combination is what I bring to a leadership role. I can set the strategy, govern the investment, and work credibly with the people building it.

I hold an MBA, an M.S. in Management Information Systems and a B.S. in Business & Accounting, with PMP, Professional Scrum Master, AWS Cloud Practitioner and FinOps certifications. The fastest way to reach me is email.
about.quote: I’ve never been satisfied with just understanding how something works. I want to know how to make it better.

experience.description: Design and build AI products independently, from product strategy and architecture through implementation and deployment: AuthMatch AI (prior-authorization review support), Prepera (career preparation), SanctionsWatch and a regulatory intelligence platform (regulatory monitoring), Gen4Me, and a supervised AI engineering system. Every product keeps a human decision-maker in the loop.

Senior PMO business partner for Apple and Dell technology programs. Shipped an automated, NIST 800-88 compliant data-deletion solution for decommissioned government laptops that cut human error by 90%, and led automation and modernization initiatives worth about $5M in annual savings.

Led delivery of retail-energy platforms across business, technology, compliance, and vendor teams. SAP billing enhancements cut annual operating costs by $500K, and a PCI-compliant IVR payment system expanded secure self-service while reducing average call-handling time by 20%.
Led the $29.4M fiber expansion program, improving communications throughput by 40%, and governed $8M in capital-project budgets across engineering, operations, vendors, and field teams.

Produced predictive intelligence assessments and delivered classified briefings to senior leaders, translating complex findings into clear recommended actions. Supervised and developed junior analysts.

paragraphs: Your name and email address, the type of inquiry you choose, and your answers to that inquiry type's questions. Depending on the type, these can include your organization, role or project details, links you add, budget, timeframe and similar business details you choose to enter.
Each message also includes the inquiry type, the page you sent it from, the audience view you were reading, the time it was received, and the version of the privacy acknowledgment you accepted.
The site does not store submissions in a database. Each one is sent as an email, and the message then exists in the recipient's mailbox and with the email provider.

sections.title: How your information is used and where it goes
paragraphs: To understand your request and reply to it, using the email address you provide.

Leadership opportunity, product or partnership, and general inquiries go to Erick directly. Strategic advisory, build-a-product, and speaking or training inquiries go to a business inbox for Clark Strategic Systems LLC. Commercial inquiries of these kinds may be handled through Clark Strategic Systems LLC.

sections.title: Service providers
paragraphs: Contact form messages are delivered by email through Resend.

To limit abuse, the form keeps short-lived counters in a Redis database. Counters are keyed to a one-way hash of your IP address, not the address itself. The form also uses a hidden field and a minimum-time check to filter automated submissions.
The site is hosted on Vercel.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: The site includes Vercel Web Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights to measure aggregate traffic and page performance. Vercel documents that Web Analytics uses no third-party cookies and identifies visitors by a hash created from the incoming request, and that Speed Insights data is not tied to an individual visitor or IP address. Data points include page URL, referrer, approximate location, browser, operating system and device type.
The site itself does not set cookies for visitors. A sign-in cookie exists only for the site owner's administrative area.

sections.title: Health and sensitive information
paragraphs: The contact form does not ask for health information. Please do not include protected health information, passwords, government IDs or confidential business documents in a message.

sections.title: How long information is kept
paragraphs: Messages are kept while we are in conversation and deleted within 90 days after it ends, unless they lead to a working relationship.
The form's abuse-prevention counters expire on their own within 10 minutes (per visitor) and 24 hours (site-wide). Analytics data is kept under Vercel's retention policy.

sections.title: Visitors outside the United States
paragraphs: Your message is used because you asked for a reply, which is a legitimate interest in answering it. The service providers named above may process it in the United States.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Reasonable technical measures protect the site and its messages. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: This site is for professional inquiries and is not directed to children under 13.

sections.title: Your choices and requests
paragraphs: You can ask what you have sent through this site, ask for a correction, or ask for deletion by emailing {email}. Requests are answered within 30 days.
Your information is never sold or shared for advertising.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: Updates are posted on this page with a new date.
